units: <cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 12:8">Kel. XII, 8</cite> <he>מטוט׳</he> Ar. a. Mish. (some ed. <he>מטוטלית</he>; ed. Dehr. <he>מְטוֹטָלוֹת</he>; Talm. ed. <he>מטולטלת</he>); <cite ref="Tosefta Keilim Batra 7:12">Tosef. Kel. B. Bath. VII, 12</cite> <he>מְטַלְטְלוֹת</he>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Kilayim 6:9">Kil. VI, 9</cite> <he>כאילו מ׳ תלויה וכ׳</he> (Ms. M. <he>מטול׳</he>) as if a plumb-line were suspended on it (take the vertical line).

senses.gloss: stem with foliage attached to a fruit.—Pl. מְטוֹטְלוֹת (cmp. טוֹטַלְוָותָא).
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah 1:5:2">Y. Ab. Zar. I, 39ᵈ</cite> <he>איצטרובלין במְטוֹטְלוֹתֵיהֶן</he> pine cones with their attachments (so that they can be used for the thyrsus, v. Sm. Ant. s. v. Thyrsus).

senses.gloss: (cmp. מַטְלִית) a pad or cushion made of pieces of cloth.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 5:3">Sabb. V, 3</cite> <he>לא יצא גמל במ׳</he> the camel must not be taken out (on the Sabbath) with the pad on his back; expl. Y. ib. 7ᵇ bot., v. <cite ref="C00096"><he>גְּבִינְתָּא</he></cite>. Bab. ib. 54ᵃ <he>במ׳ הקשורה בזנבו</he> the pad tied only to his tail (hence liable to slide down); Tosef. ib. IV (V), 3 <he>במ׳ התלויה וכ׳</he> with the pad hanging (loosely lying) on his hump to let the air strike through; ib. [read:] <he>אבל יוצא הוא במ׳ הקשורה לו בזנבו ובחטרתו וכ׳</he>.—
<cite ref="Mishnah Tamid 5:4">Tam. V, 4</cite> <he>כמין מ׳ וכ׳</he> there was on the top of the lid (of the coal pan) a sort of pad (with which to handle it).

<cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 6:7">Tosef. Sabb. VI</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 7:1">VII</cite>), 1 <he>הקושר מ׳ וכ׳</he> he who ties a pad to his hip (a superstitious custom).—Pl. <he>מְטוֹטְלוֹת מְטוֹלְטְלוֹת</he>, v. supra.
